findings.evidence: `CartanMatrix.B` is `Matrix.of fun i j => if i = j then 2 else if i.val+1 = j.val then (if j.val = n-1 then -2 else -1) else if j.val+1 = i.val then -1 else 0` (mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Cartan.lean:128); Mathlib exposes only `B_diag`/`B_off_diag_nonpos`, so each site re-derives the entry from the raw body.
findings.fix: Prove one private lemma, e.g. `(-CartanMatrix.B (n+1) j.castSucc i.castSucc).toNat = if i.val + 1 = j.val ∨ j.val + 1 = i.val then 1 else 0` (plus the two mixed `last`/`castSucc` shapes), with `simp only [CartanMatrix.B, Matrix.of_apply, Fin.ext_iff]` and a terminal `omega`/`split_ifs`, and reuse it at all five sites.
findings.issue: The same Cartan-entry computation is repeated three times (lines 162-166, 171-175, 179-183) as `simp [CartanMatrix.B, Matrix.of_apply, Fin.ext_iff]` followed by a non-terminal `omega`; the `omega` depends on whatever goal shape the default simp set leaves after unfolding Mathlib's `B` if-chain, and the same unfolding is redone inline in the branches at lines 142 and 152.

findings.evidence: Lines 97-123 already provide exactly this structure for the long-long case (`lie_typeBSimpleRootMatrix_castSucc_of_nonadjacent`, `lie_lie_typeBSimpleRootMatrix_castSucc_of_adjacent`), used at lines 168, 177, 185; the terminal branches get no such lemma.
findings.fix: Mirror the treatment of the long-long case: state named private lemmas for the short/long brackets (adjacent: `⁅e_short, ⁅e_short, e_long⁆⁆ = 0` resp. `⁅e_long, ⁅e_long, e_short⁆⁆ = 0`; non-adjacent: the plain bracket vanishes), then compute the exponent via the lemma from the previous finding and `rw [hpow, pow_one/pow_zero]` before applying them.
findings.issue: The two mixed short/long branches (lines 137-145 and 147-155) close the mathematically substantive cases — including the terminal double edge, where the exponent is 2 and `pow_two, Module.End.mul_apply` are needed to expand `ad ^ 2` — with `split_ifs <;> simp_all [...] <;> omega`, mixing the Cartan-entry case split with the matrix-unit computation over many branches. Nothing in the script shows which branch proves the double-edge relation, and `simp_all` rewrites the `hjn`/`hj` hypotheses that `omega` then consumes. This is also what pushes the proof to 59 lines (128-186).

summary: The long-long branches are cleanly factored into named helper lemmas, but the two terminal short/long branches — which carry the actual double-edge content — are discharged by an opaque `split_ifs <;> simp_all [...] <;> omega` blast, and the `CartanMatrix.B` exponent computation is duplicated three times as a non-terminal `simp` followed by `omega`.
